findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I'm approving this RED. The attested run used the exact command from the plan (`--test-name-pattern="real profile produces complete verifiable evidence"`). It exited with code 1 and was not ended by a signal or timeout. The expected-failure text matched the full stdout, which was not truncated. The failure comes from inside `expectCompleteObservation`, after the candidate was prepared successfully. The CLI rejected the `proof observe-bounded-delivery` operands with CLI_ARGUMENT_INVALID because the public `proof` command doesn't exist yet. That is the missing behavior the scenario targets, not a problem with syntax, imports, fixtures or the tools.  The proof covers both sides of the scenario. For the "When", it runs the real CLI against a clean committed full-repository candidate. For the "Then", it checks the command, candidate, runtime, inputs and complete results. It then confirms the full report bytes match their retained hash and that each of the 46 distinct required assertions appears exactly once with a passed status. Finally, it verifies the returned attempt ID through the public verification command. The mapping it checks against has 37 cases and 46 distinct results, matching the plan.  I found nothing blocking, but there are three non-blocking notes below.

This test alone can't tell real work from faked results. It checks the report against the hash the CLI itself returns, and it checks the reported runner command, but nothing shows the runner actually ran. An implementation that wrote a made-up JSON report listing all 46 assertions as passed would still pass this test. The plan relies on a separate control in step 3: remove one required result where the subprocess output is produced, and the observer must refuse. That control is needed before this proof can count as evidence of real reconciliation.

The test checks results against `.project/tickets/PPHQN5-.../evidence/proposed-assertion-map.json`, which the plan says will also be used to build the shipped profile. If an edit changes both the map and the profile, the test's oracle drifts with the code it is checking. The hardcoded count of 37 and the fixed list of expected files limit this, but only partly. Add the feature-compiled exact-set check against the 37 cases that the plan calls for.

The run used Node v24.3.0. The plan's Implementation Inspiration section pins Node 24.18.1 as the target API. This doesn't affect whether the RED failed for the right reason. Still, the GREEN run and the actual-checkout pilot should record which toolchain `scripts/dev` actually resolves.
